newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Iron talk from SBJ.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - Iron talk from SBJ.

text.p: London market broker Steel Burrill Jones tries to be optimistic in its 1996 results statement today, but a 61 percent fall in profits and an increasingly difficult operating environment tend to make an impression no matter how cheery the attempts at disguise.

The group has been racked by defections over the last two years, most recently when 13 quit its marine energy division to join Windsor Insurance. Earlier, most of its non-marine reinsurance team left.
Share price performance has been equally dismal, with the exception of a slight revival in the middle of last year.
SBJ has tried to replace staff by headhunting from Jardines and other groups, and the group recently recruited two cargo brokers.

Surprisingly, chairman Clive Richards says he sees benefits for SBJ from recent consolidation among major brokers, which includes the formation of two mega-brokers - J&H Marsh & McLennan - in that last three months. He also hinted that SBJ is trying to pick up staff that others have discarded.

Richards adds that he wants the firm to remain independent and boost business. Coincidentally it is one of the few broking firms that has not been mentioned in potential speculation, although SBJ did go through a series of take-over talk in 1995 which were fruitless.

The real problem in pursuing this line is that all its competitors have gotten bigger and, while bigger is not in every way better, they may be able to operate with lower costs, better service, and wider global reach. Competing against all this in a soft market will not be easy.
